The ASV's southward renders מִנֶּגֶב alone; אֶל has no English word of its own (rule 40). The competing reading folds אֶל מִן into one fused unit, but rule 30's fusion is for an expression the ASV renders with one word covering every morpheme's sense, and the directional אֶל adds nothing to southward that מִן has not already said.

review_notes: Both directive-he tokens (s012, s026, s031) take the ASV's to under rule 32 rather than going unrepresented, since the ASV writes a word of its own for the motion in each case.

The two occurrences of מִנֶּגֶב are read differently on purpose: the first is fused into southward (one English word, rule 30), the second is split as by / the south because the ASV spends a word on the preposition itself.
